title: AuditEvent
description: The audit event contract — Audit doc §63 field set plus the hash-chain link. Stored events are never reinterpreted in place; a new contract version is a new variant.

oneOf.description: Version 1 of the audit event contract.

timestamp.description: When the event happened — UTC, from the injected clock.

ActionOrigination.description:
How an action originated — the human-vs-system distinction Audit doc §8
requires so automation never "appear[s] as though a human personally
performed" it.

oneOf.description: Initiated by a human.
Approved by a human.
Generated by the system.
Produced by an automated workflow.
Produced by an external integration.
AI-assisted work.
AI-generated content.

ActorClassification.description:
Top-level classification of an audit actor — the spec sample's
`Human | Service | Automation | External` grouping.

Integrity rule 5 requires "human, automated, AI, integration, and
system actions" to be distinguishable: the top-level classification
groups them, and the finer-grained [`ActorKind`] (§7) plus
[`ActionOrigination`] (§8) on [`ActorRecord`] preserve the
distinctions.

oneOf.description: A person.
A service account or system process acting on its own behalf.
An automated workflow or AI agent.
An actor outside the platform — an external integration or party.

ActorId.description:
Identifies the actor behind an event — Audit doc §7: the platform
never records a bare "User changed value" without saying who or
what did it.

ActorKind.description:
Who or what performed an action. Variants are the Audit doc §7 list,
verbatim.

oneOf.description: The business owner.
A co-owner of the business.
An engaged professional (CPA, attorney, valuation, …).
An employee of the business.
A lender.
A trustee.
An external buyer.
A platform administrator.
A service account.
An automated workflow.
An AI agent.
An external integration.
A system process.

ActorRecord.description:
The `actor` field of the audit event contract (Audit doc §63): who or
what acted, identified and classified.

actor_id.description: Stable identifier for the actor (user id, service account name, …).

kind.description: Finer-grained actor kind (Audit doc §7), when known.

origination.description: How the action originated (Audit doc §8), when known.

AuditEventType.description:
The kind of material change an event records.

Variant names are engine-namespaced by prefix, per the spec sample
(`ScenarioConflictDetected` belongs to the scenario engine). New
variants join as additive cases as engines land; reorganizing existing
variants is a new [`AuditEvent`] contract version, never an edit of
stored values (Audit doc integrity rule 12).

oneOf.description: An owner decision was recorded (Audit doc §17 example event).
A scenario changed (Audit doc §17 example event).

A correction created a new event referencing the original —
integrity rule 13: "Corrections create additional events rather
than rewriting history".

The Business Reality engine recorded a new fact or the first
version of one (crate `reality`).

A Business Reality fact was revised — a new fact version
superseding the previous one; the previous version is retained,
never edited (Business Reality doc §25).

A destination version was created — either the destination's first
version or a new version from a material edit (Destination Engine
doc §26: "Every material change creates a new version").

The owner explicitly confirmed the destination — "This is the
outcome I'm trying to create" (Destination Engine doc §6).

The owner kept the destination as a working draft at the
destination checkpoint (Destination Builder doc §17).

The destination was archived — retained historically but no longer
active (Destination Engine doc §6).

A document entered the local vault (Vault doc §45: "Document
imported").

A new immutable document version was created (Vault doc §45:
"Version created"; §14: "Versioning is mandatory").

Local vault analysis ran over a document (Vault doc §45: "Document
analyzed").

An encrypted backup of the vault was exported (Vault doc §45:
"Backup completed"; §35: "The Vault should support encrypted
backups").

A scenario family was created — the birth of one conceptual path,
whether by the owner's explorer or by a what-if branch (Scenario
Engine Data Model doc §3; event contract §3.1).

A conflict was recorded against a scenario version — including
structured nonnegotiable conflicts, which carry the destination
back-reference instead of a warning flag (Scenario Engine Data
Model doc §16; event contract §3.4).

A conflict's resolution was recorded — for nonnegotiable
conflicts, the owner's decision (keep / explore another path /
change the requirement), never an engine decision (NONNEGOTIABLE
doc §5; event contract §3.5).

A what-if branch was created from a parent scenario version; the
parent is untouched (Scenario Engine Data Model doc §30–31; event
contract §3.6).

A scenario version was found pinned to Business Reality or
destination state that has since moved; the version itself is not
modified (Scenario Engine Data Model doc §35; event contract §3.7).

A durable comparison was recorded — what was compared, never which
scenario won (Scenario Engine Data Model doc §32, integrity rule
10; event contract §3.8).

A professional review reference was recorded — always attributed
to a role and identity; it never marks the scenario approved
(Scenario Engine Data Model doc §27, §29; event contract §3.9).

A scenario family was archived — retention, not deletion; every
version and its history remain readable (Scenario Engine Data
Model doc §3; event contract §3.11).

CausationId.description:
Names the immediate event that caused this one (Audit doc §19) — the
direct causal chain, distinct from correlation.

CorrelationId.description:
Groups related activity under one identifier (Audit doc §18: "Show me
everything that happened because of this change").

EngineId.description: The engine that produced an event or owns an object.

oneOf.description: Audit / provenance engine — the append-only event store (crate `audit`).
Local vault — the encrypted document workspace (crate `vault`).

Destination engine — the journey's persistent North Star (crate
`destination`).
Journey runtime — walks the EOJ journey definition (crate `journey`).
Business Reality — owner-reported facts (crate `reality`).
Scenario engine — families, versions, conflicts (crate `scenario`).
Professional review package assembly and export (crate `package`).
The Tauri shell itself (crate `app`).

EventId.description: Identifies one audit event. ULID generation lands with the audit store.

ObjectId.description:
Identifies the source object an event is about (Audit doc §6: "Source
object"); version lineage per Audit doc §21.

PayloadRef.description:
Hash-addressed reference to bulk data (Audit doc §63 field
`payload_reference`; spec: "hash-addressed, never inline bulk data").

Payloads live behind their digest — that is what keeps audit events small
and history verifiable.

digest.description: Digest of the referenced payload bytes.

Sha256Hex.description:
A lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 digest (exactly 64 hex characters).

Validation runs on construction *and* on deserialization, so a value read
from disk can never hold a malformed digest.

TransactionId.description:
Identifies the transaction (multi-event unit of work) an event
belongs to — Audit doc §63 field `transaction_id`.

WorkspaceId.description:
Identifies the workspace ("Organization/workspace", Audit doc §6) an
event or object belongs to.
